tasks.title: Lecture #17
tasks.instruction: Listen to a part of talk on astronomy.
tasks.transcript:
Thank you. It's great to see so many of you interested in this series on "Survival in Outer Space." Please excuse the cameras, we're being videotaped for the local TV stations. Tonight I'm going to talk about the most basic aspect of survival --- the space suit. When most of you imagine an astronaut, that's probably the fist thing that comes to mind, right? Well, without spaces suits, it would not be possible for us to survive in space. For example, outer space is a vacuum --- there's no gravity or air pressure; without protection, a body would explode.
What's more, we'd cook in the sun or freeze in the shade --- with temperatures ranging from a toasty 300 degrees above to a cool 300 degrees below zero Fahrenheit. The space suit that NASA has developed is truly a marvel. This photo enlargement here is a life-size image of an actual space suit worn by astronauts on the last space shuttle mission. This part is the torso --- it's made of seven extremely durable layers. This thick insulation protects against temperature extremes and radiation.
Next is what they call a "bladder" of oxygen --- that's an inflatable sac, filled with oxygen, to simulate atmospheric pressure. This bladder presses against the body with the same force as the Earth's atmosphere at sea level. The innermost layers provide liquid cooling and ventilation. Despite all the layers, the suit is flexible, allowing free movement so we can work. Another really sophisticated part of the space suit is the helmet. I brought one along to show you. Can I have a volunteer come and demonstrate?

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.B: The design and importance of the space suit
options.D: The training of astronauts for space missions

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：这段讲话的主题是什么？ 定位原文： Tonight I'm going to talk about the most basic aspect of survival — the space suit. ... Without spaces suits, it would not be possible for us to survive in space. ... The space suit that NASA has developed is truly a marvel. This photo enlargement here is a life-size image of an actual space suit worn by astronauts on the last space shuttle mission. This part is the torso — it's made of seven extremely durable layers. ... Next is what they call a "bladder" of oxygen ... Another really sophisticated part of the space suit is the helmet. 选项分析： A. The history of space exploration（太空探索的历史）。讲话未讨论太空探索的历史，所以A选项错误。 B. The design and importance of the space suit（太空服的设计和重要性）。讲话围绕太空服的各个部分（躯干、氧气囊、头盔）展开，并强调其对于在太空中生存的重要性，因此B选项正确。 C. The dangers of outer space（外太空的危险）。讲话虽提到太空的真空和极端温度，但这是为了说明太空服的必要性，并非主题，所以C选项错误。 D. The training of astronauts for space missions（宇航员为太空任务进行的训练）。基于讲话未涉及宇航员训练，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what is one of the main purposes of the "bladder" of oxygen in the space suit?

options.A: To regulate the astronaut's body temperature
options.B: To simulate the pressure of Earth's atmosphere
options.C: To protect the astronaut from solar radiation
options.D: To allow astronauts to breathe in space

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：根据演讲者，太空服中氧气“囊”的主要目的之一是什么？ 定位原文： Next is what they call a "bladder" of oxygen — that's an inflatable sac, filled with oxygen, to simulate atmospheric pressure. This bladder presses against the body with the same force as the Earth's atmosphere at sea level. 选项分析： A. To regulate the astronaut's body temperature（调节宇航员的体温）。讲话中提到调节体温的是最内层（innermost layers），而非氧气囊，所以A选项错误。 B. To simulate the pressure of Earth's atmosphere（模拟地球大气层的压力）。讲话明确指出氧气囊的作用是模拟大气压力，对身体的压力与海平面地球大气压力相同，因此B选项正确。 C. To protect the astronaut from solar radiation（保护宇航员免受太阳辐射）。讲话中提到抵御极端温度和辐射的是由七层组成的躯干部分，而非氧气囊，所以C选项错误。 D. To allow astronauts to breathe in space（让宇航员在太空中呼吸）。讲话提到氧气囊中充满氧气，但其主要功能是模拟压力，而非提供呼吸所需的氧气，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what is one feature of the space suit that allows astronauts to work effectively in space?

options.A: The suit is equipped with a cooling system.
options.B: The suit is lightweight, making it easy to carry.
options.C: The suit is flexible, allowing free movement.
options.D: The suit has a built-in communication system.

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：根据演讲者，太空服的哪个特点使宇航员能够在太空中有效工作？ 定位原文： Despite all the layers, the suit is flexible, allowing free movement so we can work. 选项分析： A. The suit is equipped with a cooling system（太空服配备了冷却系统）。讲话提到最内层提供液体冷却和通风，但并未将其与有效工作直接关联，所以A选项错误。 B. The suit is lightweight, making it easy to carry（太空服很轻便，便于携带）。基于讲话未提及太空服的重量，所以B选项错误。 C. The suit is flexible, allowing free movement（太空服具有灵活性，允许自由活动）。讲话明确指出尽管有多层结构，太空服仍然灵活，允许自由活动以便工作，因此C选项正确。 D. The suit has a built-in communication system（太空服内置了通信系统）。讲话未提及通信系统，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What is the speaker’s attitude toward the space suit?

options.A: The speaker is impressed by the complexity and design of the suit.
options.B: The speaker believes the space suit needs improvement.
options.C: The speaker feels that the space suit is too uncomfortable for astronauts.
options.D: The speaker thinks the space suit is outdated and inefficient.

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：演讲者对太空服持什么态度？ 定位原文： The space suit that NASA has developed is truly a marvel. ... This part is the torso — it's made of seven extremely durable layers. ... Another really sophisticated part of the space suit is the helmet. 选项分析： A. The speaker is impressed by the complexity and design of the suit（演讲者对太空服的复杂性和设计印象深刻）。讲话用“truly a marvel”“extremely durable”“really sophisticated”等词表达赞赏，因此A选项正确。 B. The speaker believes the space suit needs improvement（演讲者认为太空服需要改进）。基于讲话未提出改进建议，所以B选项错误。 C. The speaker feels that the space suit is too uncomfortable for astronauts（演讲者觉得太空服对宇航员来说太不舒服了）。讲话未讨论舒适度问题，所以C选项错误。 D. The speaker thinks the space suit is outdated and inefficient（演讲者认为太空服过时且效率低下）。讲话表达的是赞赏而非批评，所以D选项错误。
